title_original: ‘Hunger Games’ rules UK-Ireland box office with £9.9m as ‘You Can See Everything’ sets records
excerpt_original: ‘Sunrise…’ scores 4th-biggest opening of 2026; ‘Ramayana’ becomes biggest Indian film of all time.

Lionsgate’s The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping lit up the UK-Ireland box office with a £9.9m opening weekend – the fourth biggest of the year.
Opening in 664 sites, it took a substantial £14,900 location average. Its £9.9m start is behind only Spider-Man: Brand New Day (£23.5m), Toy Story 5 (£14.4m) and The Odyssey (£12.6m).

It is the second biggest Friday-to-Sunday opening of The Hunger Games franchise, behind 2013’s Catching Fire (£10.1m). However, Sunrise On The Reaping also took a sizeable £3.2m from previews – enough to top the chart on its own – for a £13m full opening, which is above the £12.2m full start of Catching Fire .

It is a biggest ever full opening for Lionsgate UK, ahead of Hunger Games stablemates Mockingjay, Part 1 (£12.7m), Catching Fire and Mockingjay, Part 2 (£11.3m). Catching Fire became the highest-grossing of those titles, and Lionsgate’s highest in the territory, with £34.2m. With Sunrise already over 38% of the way to that mark, it will harbour hopes of setting a new high bar for the distributor.

Despite the record-breaking rollout of the Grand Theft Auto VI video game, it was a weekend of multiple successes in cinemas. A24’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything opened in second place to £2.5m, from 596 sites at a £4,118 average, with several sites still to report. Holdover is handling UK-Ireland distribution for A24.

This is the biggest opening ever for a non-music documentary, with almost double the £1.3m of 2004s Fahrenheit 9/11 . It is also the fourth biggest documentary opening of all time, behind Michael Jackson film This Is It (£4.9m), One Direction: This Is Us (£3.5m) and 2026’s Oasis: Don’t Look Back In Anger (£2.7m), not including event cinema concert films such as Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour (£5.7m).

blocks.text: The film is already the 12 th -highest-grossing documentary of all time in the UK and Ireland, after just three days in cinemas; and is A24’s fourth-highest grossing release, behind Backrooms (£13.2m), Everything Everywhere All At Once (£6m) and The Whale (£3.5m).

Paramount’s Ebenezer dropped from first to third after a £2.3m second weekend, down 41% on its opening. It is now up to £8.1m total, and should overtake the £10m of fellow Johnny Depp title Alice Through The Looking Glass from 2016 in the next week.
Having expanded wide on the previous weekend, Entertainment Film Distributors’ I Play Rocky added £504,000 on its third session, with the 56% drop taking it to £3.3m total.

Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend has become the highest-grossing Indian film of all time at the UK-Ireland box office. The Sony release added £338,000 – a 69% drop – to hit £4.8m, overtaking the £4.5m of this year’s Dhurandhar: The Revenge and £4.4m of 2023’s Pathaan .

Boosted by Sunrise On The Reaping , takings for the top five titles jumped 106% on last weekend. The figures are down 31% on the equivalent weekend from last year, when Wicked: For Good posted a huge £17.8m start. However, that film dropped off relatively quickly; should Sunrise … and You Can See Everything show staying power, cinemas will still be in a good position heading towards December, with Paramount’s Focker-In-Law (November 25) and Disney’s Hexed (November 27) to come this week.
Trafalgar trio

Wild Horse Nine leads Disney’s slate, with a £375,000 third weekend in cinemas. Martin McDonagh’s film fell 59% on its previous session, and is up to £3.6m total, topping the £3.2m total of the director’s 2012 film Seven Psychopaths .
Wicker dropped out of the top five on its fourth weekend in cinemas, falling 68% for Black Bear with £212,000 taking it to £6.5m total.

The filmed release of Mark Rosenblatt’s play Giant , starring John Lithgow as Roald Dahl, took £162,000 from 462 sites at a £351 average. Including screenings since Thursday, it is at £373,000 lifetime for Trafalgar Releasing.
On its second weekend in cinemas, Trafalgar stablemate Festive Fun With Peppa added £155,000, down 37%, and is up to £440,000.
Ghosts: The Possession Of Button House is now Lionsgate’s highest-grossing UK production ever with £8.8m, overtaking Eddie The Eagle (£8.7m) after a £129,000 fifth session.

blocks.text: Concert film BTS World Tour ‘Arirang’ In Kaohsiung brought in £127,000 from 200 sites for Trafalgar Releasing, at a £633 average and mainly from Saturday screenings.
Primetime starring new James Bond Robert Pattinson added £122,000 on its fourth weekend in cinemas, down 73% and up to £4.5m in total.
On its third weekend in cinemas, La Bola Negra added £112,000 for Altitude, and is up to £1.4m in a strong result for a film not in the English language.
Source: DreamWorks
‘Forgotten Island’
Forgotten Island now leads Universal’s slate, after a £109,000 sixth weekend – down 53%, but holding better than many box office rivals. The Philippines-set animation has £6m across its run.

Park Circus’s Arthur Christmas re-release took £109,000 from 151 sites at a healthy £719 average. The animation totalled £21.4m on its original 2011 run, with a further £229,000 on a 10 th -anniversary re-release.
A Talent For Murder starring Helen Mirren as author Patricia Highsmith started with £104,000 from 353 sites for Universal, at a £294 average, and with £131,000 including previews.
Bassam Tariq’s Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother started with £104,000 from 215 sites at a £484 average for Amazon MGM Studios, with £170,000 including previews.

links.text: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother

blocks.text: Godzilla Minus Zero has overtaken 2023 first film Godzilla Minus One (£2.6m total. It added £93,500 for Anime Ltd, down 81% from its previous session and up to £2.8m from three sessions.
Stop motion animation Wildwood put on £89,000 on its fifth weekend in cinemas for Black Bear, after falling 63%. Travis Knight’s film is up to £4.2m total.
Clayface is Warner Bros’ standout title in cinemas, with £85,700 on its fifth session in cinemas and £7m total. Its drop of just 12% was significantly better than this weekend’s market average.
Christmas special screenings are increasing in number at the box office, with CBeebies Panto 2026: Treasure Island taking in £71,700 from 381 sites at a £188 average for Vue Lumière.

Fjord is now Cristian Mungiu’s highest-grossing film of all time, after added £40,700 on its second session with a 67% drop and £369,000 total for Picturehouse Entertainment. It overtook the £301,000 of Mungiu’s first Palme d’Or winner 4 Months, 3 Weeks, 2 Days .
Shaun The Sheep: The Beast Of Mossy Bottom leads Studiocanal’s slate, with £32,300 on its 10 th weekend in cinemas taking it beyond the £6m mark.

blocks.text: BFI Distribution’s release of the restoration of Ken Russell’s The Devils is up to £721,000 after a £23,600 fourth session.
David Leitch’s crime comedy How To Rob A Bank sank on its second weekend, dropping 91% with £23,200 bringing it to £436,000. Sony handles distribution for the Amazon MGM Studios film.
George Michael: The Faith Tour sung out another £20,200 on its third weekend in cinemas, taking it to £1.8m cume.
Sundance title Josephine started with £17,300 for Curzon, from 52 sites at a £334 average. The drama has £48,800 including previews.
Sony’s Prima Facie starring Cynthia Erivo added £15,700 on its second session after a steep 92% drop, and is up to £367,000.

Rafael Manuel’s Film4-backed UK title Filipiñana opened to £14,200 for BFI Distribution, from just six cinemas. This brought it an excellent £2,370 average, with the film up to £22,800 including previews.
Animation Tad And The Magic Lamp put on £11,400 on its fifth session for Paramount, with a £740,000 lifetime.
On its fifth weekend in cinemas, Pawel Pawlikowski’s Fatherland added £11,200 for Mubi to hit £883,000 cume.

Former number one Resident Evil scared up a further £8,560 on its 10 th session in cinemas, and is up to £14.8m for Sony, with more than three times the £4.8m of the next title in the franchise, 2010’s Resident Evil: Afterlife .
Paramount’s Street Fighter kicked up a further £7,000 on its sixth weekend in cinemas, and is up to a £6.2m cume.
Rob Savage’s Other Mommy put on £5,520 on its seventh weekend in cinemas for Universal, with £5.6m across its run.
Brad Pitt-starrer Heart Of The Beast is closing out for Paramount after nine weekends in cinemas, with £3,000 on its latest session bringing it to a £7.5m total.
Verity starring Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson put on £2,590 on its eighth session. The Amazon MGM Studios film, distributed by Sony, is just below £12m across its run.
